scope: Finite same-owner native vehicle casualty intent, replacement seat and original-goal acknowledgement
implementation: Current owner brain may retain its already admitted native vehicle goal through driver death/removal. Route provenance alone grants no speed or recovery authority. Unknown live replacement seats invalidate the old transition; exact pending candidate is recognised.

Existing bounded native Eject/MoveToDriver crew path handles the vacancy with its original25-second journal, assignment/role/task/Zeus/provider/care/physical-rest guards and at most20 crew. Exact prior cap cleanup must settle before native seat actions. Active recovery work refuses this path.

A confirmed replacement seat either already has the original MOVE goal or receives that goal once on its current local operating owner. RETURNING observes both operating actors; at most2 seconds within original crew deadline, no replay. New leader/operator MOVE or STOP wins.

Exact current brain/journal/seat/goal acknowledgement atomically rebinds the native operating receipt. Ordinary driving assistance waits while native crew work is pending. Existing route-scoped jam/geometry context detects the changed operating receipt.

A vacancy after COMPLETE is a distinct episode, including removed driver objects. CANCELLED/EXPIRED vacancy attempts do not restart on each callback. Healthy-driver cheap path and authored remote-vehicle seat action policy retained.

After crew callouts, current brain/owner identity is checked again before assistance or diagnostics. Native casualty transitions also recheck the possibly rebound route, preventing a cancelled/superseded seat episode from driving under an old generation.
